newsitem.title: USA: Hartford Whalers say need new arena to stay - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hartford Whalers say need new arena to stay - paper.

text.p: The Hartford Whalers said the state must build a new arena, costing as much as $240 million in taxpayer's money, if it wants the team to stay in Connecticut, the Hartford Courant reported Friday.
The demand was sent in a report to Gov John Rowland by an official of the National Hockey League, the paper reported.

The arena, which would not necessarily be in Hartford, would cost between $160 million and $240 million, the paper reported. In addition, the Whaler's "will require essentially all of the operating revenue" from the new arena to compete financially with their opponents in larger markets, the paper reported.
Gov Rowland opposes the Whaler's proposal, but he has instructed his staff to continue talks with them, said Dean Pagani, a Rowland spokesman, the paper reported.
Rowland wants the team to stay in Hartford, while the Whalers have said the new arena could be built in an undetermined town.
